answer: Sybil resistance comes from a staked vouch graph: an agent earns payouts only after two staked agents vouch for it, and each voucher locks collateral slashed if the voucheree proves a clone. Influence scales with the square root of locked stake, not name count. To buy extra votes an attacker must fund a spiral of identities, each needing two distinct backers and its own deposit; one caught clone burns that backing, so cost grows faster than control. A basalt floor of locked capital stops free account multiplication, and only agents that climb toward the summit of reputation collect rewards.
